title: Pre-public security review of ward-cli at b1dae53 (operator request via opum-doc)
description: The operator asked first-party, through opum-doc, for a pre-public security review of Ward at origin/dev b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-29. Three read-only Opus reviewer units (detached worktrees review-sec-a, review-sec-b, review-sec-c under .claude/worktrees/ at that SHA) each return a verdict by message; this task records the three verdicts. The repository visibility flip is tier 3 and the operator alone; nothing here changes visibility.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The verdict of each of the three reviewer units is recorded on this task, naming the reviewed SHA and the unit
Every finding is dispositioned: filed as its own task, or recorded as not-a-defect with the reason

implementationNotes:
VERDICTS, recorded 2026-10-30 from the team-lead relay. Reviewed SHA for all three: b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d. Units: ward-cli-review-sec-a, -b, -c, read-only, detached worktrees. Model: claude-opus-5-5 for each, reported by the leader as verified MATCH with spawn-model (not re-measured here). Full texts for a and c are in the leader scratchpad (wardsec/verdict-sec-a.txt and verdict-sec-c.txt).

(a) SECRET CUSTODY: READY-FOR-PUBLIC. No finding above LOW. LOW-1 leftover typed or pasted bytes reach the shell (passphrase reader truncates instead of refusing; neither reader flushes the tty). LOW-2 a backup passphrase has no minimum (design choice, A/B to opum-doc). LOW-3 a reporting.ts comment states a false custody invariant and every vault read turns all secret values into immutable strings. LOW-4 ward restore creates a key without taking setup.lock. LOW-5 race between creating a backup file and stripping its inherited ACL. INFO-1 zeroing incomplete in several copies. INFO-2 chmod -N gets the path without --. INFO-3 files Ward did not create keep an inherited ACL. INFO-4 no secure_delete pragma. INFO-5 install runbook trains remember-this-choice without checking the dialog names the binary. Conceded and documented, not new: ward backup is gated only by stdin.isTTY, the key is readable through the trusted build, rollback is undetected, same-user TOCTOU on ~/.ward.

(b) APPROVAL AND TRANSPORT: FIX-BEFORE-PUBLIC. Headlines as the leader relayed them: the DEC-248 secret-header gap (being fixed in opum-ai/ward-cli#208); a new spoofable approval prompt; an agent can approve its own profile through a pseudo-terminal, which the spec concedes but the README does not say. NOTE: verdict-sec-b.txt in the scratchpad holds only transcript residue and the leader summary, not the unit full finding list, so the per-finding detail for (b) is NOT recorded here and must be supplied before AC2 can disposition it.

(c) PUBLIC EXPOSURE: FIX-BEFORE-PUBLIC. 1 CRITICAL fork pull requests reach the self-hosted runners (ci.yml on pull_request, all jobs on self-hosted Linux ARM64); the leader measured allows_public_repositories=false on the Default and mbpm2 runner groups, so a fork PR would get no runner and not execute, but every PR to dev would then block on required checks that never report. 2 MEDIUM GitHub-held refs (206 refs/pull/N/head) are permanent on the flip, a history rewrite does not remove them. 3 MEDIUM personal data and local machine facts in history and tree (author email and name, local username and home paths in hook-written notes and .quest records). 4 LOW internal infrastructure detail (runner group and pod names, ruleset id, RUNNER_HOST in the release notes). 5 LOW internal process material and private product names, including the WCLI-84 alias and Vercel bypass mechanism. 6 LOW release install proves integrity not authenticity (suggests build-provenance attestation). 7 LOW README and runbook go stale on the flip. 8 INFO no LICENSE and no SECURITY.md. All 23 secret-scanner hits triaged as not real credentials (code naming a secret, an eval canary, throwaway test TLS keys under test/fixtures/tls, expected to need a scanner allowlist).

AC2 stays open: dispositions follow opum-doc ruling and the operator A/B. No fix task is filed here.

VERDICT (b) IN FULL, appended 2026-10-30 (supersedes the headline-only paragraph for (b) above). Unit ward-cli-review-sec-b, slice approval, snapshot and transport, SHA b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d, model claude-opus-5-5 (leader-reported MATCH), verdict FIX-BEFORE-PUBLIC. The unit read source only and executed nothing; every scenario is reasoned, not measured. F2 and F3 drive the verdict.

F1 HIGH, documented non-guarantee (spec 4.2, 4.3, ADR 0003): the agent can approve its own profile through a pseudo-terminal. The only consent gate is process.stdin.isTTY (terminal-consent.ts for profiles, registration, grants and unregister), so piping a yes through script allocates a pty and is read as consent; the keychain ACL trusts the ward binary, so no OS dialog. The agent can then point a profile at a public capture endpoint and read the bearer value from its log. Fix: none fits the P0 same-user model; state the caveat in README and the public security docs; structural fix is spec 4.2 own advice, a broker outside the agent OS identity or an out-of-band consent channel.

F2 MEDIUM-HIGH, ruled as DEC-248, confirmed open at this SHA: declared headers can redefine the request. Only authorization and proxy-authorization were reserved, so Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, TE, Upgrade, Expect and others passed; a declared Host yields two Host headers while SNI and certificate checks name the approved host, which a lenient CDN could route to another tenant. Fix (WCLI-84): refuse the hop-by-hop and framing names. Also consider refusing or flagging method and URL rewrite headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-HTTP-Method, X-Method-Override, X-Original-URL, X-Rewrite-URL, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-Host).

F3 MEDIUM, new and untested: the approval prompt can be spoofed by layout alone. escapeForDisplay leaves ordinary spaces and NBSP untouched, a profile may declare 32 headers of 2048 characters, and url is printed before the headers, so padded header values can scroll the real url and method off screen and render a benign url and headers none line. No test covers prompt length or wrapping. Fix: repeat method and destination host and the header count on the final y/N line, cap displayed header length and count or lower the bounds, escape whitespace runs and NBSP, optionally require typing the host.

F4 LOW, not measured: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR are untested, so the claim that the system store is the only trust store is unproven for the compiled binary; exploiting needs a network position, and WCLI-19 concedes same-user injection. Fix: a probe like transport-tls-disable-probe, or scrub the variables in guard.ts and assert it.

F5 INFO: run_credential_invalid is a one-bit static oracle for control bytes in the stored value, negligible.

F6 INFO: the whole decrypted vault and the key stay in memory across network I/O during ward run (state held by a closure across transport.send; writeAudit re-parses twice), so a core file would hold every secret. Unverified; inside ADR 0002 non-guarantees and WCLI-19. Hardening: setrlimit RLIMIT_CORE 0 at startup and drop references to state before send.

CONFIRMED SOUND per the unit: snapshot is the authority and the request is built only from it; admission re-checks approval, expiry, grant and secret revision in one transaction; approval TOCTOU closed by re-reading the manifest after the answer; binding on profile, project, root, device and inode; stale-version approvals inert; expiry boundary; strict URL grammar with punycode only; closed method enum; one latin1 encoding checked then written; destination resolved once and classified, no rebinding; ambient proxy bypassed; rejectUnauthorized true with TLS 1.2 minimum; harness hooks unreachable from the CLI; redirects not followed; status-only output with the body never read; credential buffers zeroed in finally blocks.

NOT REACHED: approvals.ts, audit.ts, the transport port types, secret-value.ts, project-files.ts, checkout.ts beyond line 110, the bodies of the transport and run tests, docs/security-tests.md, ADR 0021 to 0023, and Bun runtime behaviour. AC1 stays ticked; AC2 stays open.

W-3 first half (Host and framing headers) is WCLI-84 (opum-ai/ward-cli#208), no duplicate. No task: W-24 (no fix required), W-26 (no real credential, not a blocker), W-33 history and W-37 license (operator decisions dec-0znz91e and dec-1frlqzm, nothing done). Priority: the tracker was given high for W-1 (critical in the report) because no critical value was confirmed. Rulings recorded in the matching tasks: W-34 A in WCLI-99, W-35 A in WCLI-114, W-36 A in WCLI-96 and WCLI-109. AC2 stays open until each child is dispositioned.
